content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide and salicylates (e.g., aspirin, choline magnesium trisalicylate): Mechanism: Increased gastric pH leads to passive renal tubular reabsorption. Effect: Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. Clinical significance: Minor; significance unknown. 2. Aluminum hydroxide and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate: Mechanism: Same as above (increased pH and passive renal tubular reabsorption). Effect: Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses. Clinical significance: Minor; significance unknown. 3. Clinical significance: Minor; significance unknown. 4. Blessed thistle and aluminum hydroxide: Mechanism: Pharmacodynamic antagonism. Effect: Decreases the effects of aluminum hydroxide. Clinical significance: Minor; theoretical interaction. 5. Aluminum hydroxide and choline magnesium trisalicylate: Mechanism: Same as above (increased pH and passive renal tubular reabsorption). Effect: Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses. Clinical significance: Minor; significance unknown. 6.
